1: Hello, I'm… — introduce myself, my job and my company
Language: be, possessive adjectives, a / an with jobs
Simulation: first day — meet the team
2: My team and my role — say who does what in my team and what I do
Language: present simple (he / she works…), there is / there are
Simulation: explain your team to a new colleague
3: My workday — describe my routine and schedule
Language: frequency adverbs, telling the time
Simulation: compare schedules to find a free slot
4: Numbers, dates and contact details — give and check numbers, dates and email addresses
Language: numbers, dates, spelling aloud, Could you repeat that?
Simulation: take down a client's contact details
5: Around the office — ask where things are and what people can do
Language: prepositions of place, can / can't
Simulation: help a new colleague find things
6: Arranging a meeting — suggest, accept and change a meeting time
Language: Are you free on…?, How about…?, days and times
Simulation: book a meeting with three busy colleagues
7: Simple emails — write a short email to ask or confirm something
Language: greetings and sign-offs, I'd like to…, Could you…?
Simulation: reply to a meeting invitation
8: Calls and video calls — start, join and end a call, and take a simple message
Language: Can you hear me?, Can I speak to…?, I'll call back
Vocabulary: mute, share my screen, connection, message
Simulation: a video call with small tech problems — then take a message
9: Last week at work — talk about what I did
Language: past simple (regular and irregular), time expressions
Simulation: Monday catch-up — what happened last week
10: A short presentation — present my team or a task in three slides
Language: first / then / finally, This slide shows…, comparatives for simple numbers
Simulation: present your team in three slides
11: Quick messages — write and answer short chat messages (Teams, WhatsApp)
Language: requests with can / could, short answers, imperatives
Vocabulary: chat words (ASAP, FYI, thanks), polite short forms
Simulation: a busy morning in the team chat
12: Small talk at the office — chat at the coffee break about the weekend and free time
Language: How was your…?, past simple questions, would like for offers
Vocabulary: free time, weekend, food and drink
Simulation: coffee break with a new colleague
13: Plans and next steps — talk about plans and arrangements
Language: going to, present continuous for future, will for offers
Simulation: plan next month's team event
14: Rules and tasks — explain what people must and should do
Language: have to / don't have to, should
Simulation: explain the rules to a new employee
15: Small problems — report a problem and apologise
Language: I'm sorry, but…, I'll… for promises
Simulation: a client calls — the delivery is late
16: My experience — talk about my experience in a short interview

1: Networking and small talk — start, keep up and end a conversation with a new contact
Vocabulary: small-talk topics, safe and unsafe topics
2: My role and my company — describe my responsibilities and my company's structure
Language: present simple vs. continuous, be responsible for, report to
Simulation: introduce your team to a new partner
3: Email essentials — write a clear request and a polite follow-up
Language: indirect questions, I was wondering if…, formal vs. neutral register
Simulation: chase a colleague who hasn't replied
4: Chat and messaging — write short, clear messages on Teams or Slack
Language: short forms, imperatives softened with please / could
Simulation: sort out a problem in a team chat
5: Video calls — start a call, ask for clarification and handle tech problems
Language: Sorry, you broke up, Could you repeat that?, Let me share my screen
Simulation: a weekly call where everything goes wrong
6: Phone calls — make and return calls and leave a voicemail
Language: I'm calling about…, Could you ask her to…?
Simulation: leave a voicemail, then return the call
7: Taking part in meetings — give updates and ask questions in a meeting
Language: present perfect for news, Just to add…
Simulation: a team meeting with an agenda
8: Language: softening (I'm not sure that…, I see your point, but…)
Simulation: decide where to hold the team event
9: Presenting: structure — open, organise and close a short talk
Language: signposting (First…, Moving on to…, To sum up…)
Simulation: 3-minute talk about your own job
10: Data and trends — describe graphs, numbers and changes
Language: rise / fall / remain, sharply / slightly, past simple
11: Customers and complaints — handle a complaint and keep the customer
Language: apologising, I'll make sure…, will for promises
Simulation: an unhappy customer on the phone
12: Problem solving — suggest and compare solutions
Language: What if we…?, We could…, first conditional
Simulation: fix a supply problem as a team
13: Project updates — report progress and delays
Language: present perfect vs. past simple, already / yet / still
Vocabulary: milestone, on track, behind schedule
14: Deadlines and priorities — prioritise, delegate and say no politely
Language: need to, I'm afraid I can't…, Could you take care of…?
Simulation: too much work — share the tasks
15: Negotiation basics — make an offer, a counter-offer and a compromise
Language: first and second conditional, If you…, we could…
Simulation: agree a price with a supplier
16: Pulling it together — run a short project from start to finish
Language: review of the module's language
Simulation: kick-off meeting for a new project

1: Pitching an idea — pitch an idea in two minutes
Language: Imagine if…, What this means for you is…, rhetorical questions
Simulation: elevator pitch to a director
2: Persuasive presentations — build a talk that ends in a decision
Language: emphasis (What we really need is…), rule of three
Simulation: present a proposal and ask for approval
3: Tough questions — handle Q&A, including hostile or off-topic questions
Language: That's a good question, buying time, deflecting politely
4: Chairing meetings — open, steer and close a meeting
Language: Let's hear from…, Can we get back to…?
Simulation: chair a meeting that keeps going off topic
5: Decision-making — weigh options and reach a team decision
Language: second conditional, On the one hand…, modals of deduction
Simulation: choose a new office location
6: Negotiation strategy — prepare and run a negotiation
Language: conditionals, hedging (We might be able to…), bargaining phrases
Simulation: renew a contract with a key client
7: Handling conflict — calm a conflict and find common ground
Language: diplomatic language, It seems to me that…, past modals
Simulation: two team members disagree on priorities
8: Feedback — give and receive feedback constructively
Language: softeners, It might be worth…, situation–behaviour–impact
Simulation: a feedback conversation with a team member
9: Coaching and delegating — delegate a task and coach someone through it
Language: What would you do if…?, have / get something done
Simulation: hand over a project to a junior colleague
10: Working across cultures — adapt my style to people from other cultures
Language: indirect vs. direct language, softening
Simulation: a call with partners from two countries
11: Writing reports — write a clear short report
Language: passive voice, however / therefore / as a result
Simulation: write a one-page report on a project
12: Writing proposals — write a persuasive proposal
Language: formal register, We propose that…, nominalisation
Simulation: write and defend a proposal
13: Career moves — do an interview and present myself on LinkedIn
Language: present perfect continuous, talking about achievements
14: Communicating change — announce a change and handle reactions
Language: We're going to…, reassuring language, future continuous
Simulation: announce a reorganisation to the team
15: Crisis communication — respond to a crisis clearly and calmly
Language: passive for neutral statements, third conditional
Simulation: a press or client statement after a problem
16: Strategy — discuss strategy and long-term goals
Language: future perfect, By next year we will have…
Simulation: plan the company's next year
